title: Gloria's Foundation debuts Gloria's Rings, an art installation by Tiffany Shlain and Jessica Kaulbacbk
summary: Gloria's Foundation opened Gloria's Rings, an art installation that debuted at the memorial for Gloria Steinem at the Park Avenue Armory in New York City on November 18, 2026. Gloria's Rings features a newly commissioned monumental sculpture by interdisciplinary artist and Emmy-nominated filmmaker Tiffany Shlain and a full-scale relief print by artist Jessica Kaulback. Shlain's work, A Dendrobiography of Gloria Steinem, is a work created from a 3,000 pound salvaged eucalyptus slab that traces the arc of Gloria's life through 92 markers of her life including facts, quotes and and poignant moments from the movement she helped found and grow. Kaulback's artwork Heartwood is a full-scale relief print of the same tree slab that serves as a meditation on strength, transformation, and the enduring impact of Steinem's life on generations to come.

title: Christie's to offer Alexander McQueen Plato's Atlantis dress from designer's final fully realized collection
summary: Christie's New York will present A Defining Vision: Plato's Atlantis, Look 4 by Alexander McQueen, an extraordinary runway creation from one of the most influential fashion collections of the 21st century. A defining work from the legendary British designer's final fully realized collection, the Dress embodies the imagination, technical brilliance, and groundbreaking artistry that established McQueen as one of the most visionary designers in fashion history. Widely regarded as a masterpiece of his career, Plato's Atlantis represented the culmination of McQueen's creative vision, transcending the traditional boundaries of fashion to become a landmark of contemporary culture. This exceptional Dress, will be part of Handbags & Fashion Online: The New York Edit and Christie's December Luxury

title: The Museo Nacional del Prado opens the first monographic exhibition in Spain devoted to Hans Baldung Grien
summary: The Museo Nacional del Prado is presenting an exhibition on Hans Baldung Grien, one of the most significant figures of the German Renaissance. It takes its starting point from the paintings Harmony (The Three Graces?) and The Ages and Death, the two works by the artist in the Museum’s permanent collection, establishing a dialogue with a group of works that allows for a deeper understanding of the artistic and intellectual context in which they were conceived. Created before 1545, during the final years of Baldung's career, the two panels articulate a complex reflection on beauty, the passage of time and death. Their recent restoration has allowed for the recovery of the compositions' rich colours and numerous botanical details, as well as providing new information on the materials and techniques and on the artist’s creative process. title: Bertoia's December 10 Holiday Auction will be a winter wonderland for collectors of Christmas antiques
summary: Bertoia’s Thursday, December 10 Holiday Auction promises a festive selection of antique Christmas, Halloween, Thanksgiving and Easter collectibles. Highlights include German Santas, belsnickels, Dresden ornaments, early glass decorations, Halloween lanterns, and papier-mâché candy containers. The auction also features an appealing assortment of Schoenhut toys, circus figures, automata, and other treasured playthings from generations past, including some wonderful American and European tin toys and other surprises. Angels, glass ornaments, and an FAO Schwarz Santa sleigh with reindeer will also be up for bid. A rare terra cotta Father Christmas figure that’s been on display in the Bertoia household for more than three decades is sure to spark a bidding war. title: Sean Scully traces five decades of abstraction in second solo show at Galerie Max Hetzler
summary: Galerie Max Hetzler, Berlin, is presenting Block, an exhibition of paintings and sculptures by Sean Scully. This is the artist’s second solo exhibition with the gallery. For Block, Scully presents a body of paintings spanning from 1974 to 2026, alongside a selection of sculptures from 2015 to 2025. The works, often vast in scale, engage in dialogue with one another. Echoes in palette, structure and form reverberate across their two- and three-dimensional surfaces. On this, the artist has stated: ‘My sculptures are my paintings 3D’.2 Across his work, Scully draws from the legacies of Henri Matisse, Piet Mondrian, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Pablo Picasso and Mark Rothko. Fusing personal influence with European tradition and American abstraction, his compositions are built layer by layer, block by block. title: RM Sotheby's to offer the first Mercedes-Benz C 111 ever brought to market
summary: RM Sotheby’s announced that Mercedes-Benz AG will offer a unique C 111-II, fitted with an original 2.4-liter four-rotor Wankel engine, at its Paris auction on February 3, 2027, held at the Palais du Louvre. This means that, for the first time in its history, Mercedes-Benz is offering a C 111 for sale—a car that was previously out of reach. For at least 25 years, this will remain the only opportunity: Mercedes-Benz has contractually committed not to sell any further C 111s during this period. The C 111 is one of the most fascinating vehicles in the brand’s history. When it was unveiled at the 1969 International Motor Show (IAA) in Frankfurt am Main, it embodied the vision of taking the design and technical innovations of the legendary 300 SL (W 198) into a new era. However, it never went into series production. In total, only 17 prototypes of the iconic super sports car were made. title: Landry Pop Auctions to present exceptional offering of Japanese Sofubi and original art
summary: Landry Pop Auctions will offer Showa / Contemporary: Japanese Sofubi & Original Art on December 1, featuring an extraordinary selection of rare vintage Japanese soft-vinyl toys, original science fiction illustrations, and contemporary sofubi creations. Bringing together historically significant examples from pioneering manufacturers Bullmark and Marusan alongside original artwork by celebrated Japanese illustrators and limited-production figures from today's leading independent makers, the sale represents a rare opportunity for collectors to acquire some of the most elusive and desirable works in Japanese pop culture. Leading the auction is an exceptionally rare 1974 Bullmark Toho Mechagodzilla Standard Vinyl (estimate: $20,000–30,000), widely regarded as one of the most coveted figures in vintage Japanese kaiju collecting. title: Buff Monster and TengaOne blend graffiti, pop culture, and social commentary in new GR gallery show
summary: GR gallery opened Disorderly Conduct, a duo exhibition featuring Buff Monster and TengaOne. Bringing together vibrant characters, pop-cultural references, and decades of graffiti-inspired techniques, the exhibition explores the uneasy intersections of consumerism, societal change, and the contradictions of human nature. Balancing urban sensibilities with highbrow aesthetics, the grotesque with the innocent, both artists construct worlds where bold colors, playful imagery, and familiar narratives conceal unsettling realities. Beneath the apparent joy, subtle tensions emerge, hinting at darker undercurrents of violence, struggle, and greed—elements often hidden in plain sight. In Disorderly Conduct, Buff Monster presents his Melty Misfits characters, the unlikely protagonists of a colorful yet imperfect universe, with a fresh twist. title: Christie's presents over 220 jewels in online 'Joaillerie Paris' sale
summary: For the latest edition of Joaillerie Paris, taking place online from 4 to 16 December, Christie's is delighted to present an exclusive selection of more than 220 jewels, perfectly suited to the festive season. The sale will feature exceptional coloured gemstones, led by a remarkable Kashmir sapphire offered with an estimate of €600,000-800,000. An iconic Van Cleef & Arpels “Ballerine” clip, a selection of creations by the leading houses of Place Vendôme – from Cartier and Boucheron to Bvlgari – as well as an outstanding group of jewels by Boivin, further enrich the sale. With estimates ranging from €2,000 to €600,000 and several lots offered without reserve, the auction is designed to appeal to a wide range of buyers just ahead of the holiday season. Clad entirely in gold and diamonds, the celebrated Ballerine clip by Van Cleef & Arpels, first introduced in New York in 1943, is one of the star lots of the sale (€80,000-120,000). title: British conceptual artist Gavin Turk explores "domestic anthropology" and the uncanny in new Hong Kong show
summary: Ben Brown Fine Arts Hong Kong presents Betwixt, an exhibition of paintings and sculpture by British artist Gavin Turk, on view from 21 November 2026 to 30 January 2027. Bringing together several distinct bodies of work, the exhibition is grounded in what Turk calls "domestic anthropology", which he describes as "the exploration of the domestic, with the question of value, and the act of re-noticing". The title comes from the archaic English word 'betwixt', which evokes being caught between two conditions – a state Turk has explored for more than three decades through his interrogation of authorship, value and belief. Works in the exhibition explore liminality, poised between presence and absence, arrival and departure. title: The New York Historical spotlights Marilyn Monroe's agency and power through the lens of Lawrence Schiller
summary: One hundred years later and America still can’t get enough of Marilyn Monroe. In honor of the centennial anniversary of the year she was born in 1926, The New York Historical presents a new exhibition on her life, career, and her lesser-known attempts to wrestle control of her legacy. On display from November 20, 2026 – March 28, 2027 in the Jean Margo Reid Center for Women’s History, Marilyn Monroe Centennial: Photographs by Lawrence Schiller juxtaposes the legendary star’s on-camera and off-camera persona with images taken by photojournalist Lawrence Schiller on two film sets: Let’s Make Love in 1960 and Monroe’s last and unfinished film Something’s Got to Give in 1962. title: Artium Museoa presents German photographer Jochen Lempert's debut show in the Basque Country
summary: Artium Museoa, Museum of Contemporary Art of the Basque Country presents the solo exhibition Local Ecology (A1 Gallery, until 29 March 2027) by Jochen Lempert (Moers, Germany, 1958, living and working in Hamburg). The exhibition brings together earlier series of his work and includes photographs taken during his visit to Álava in June of this year. The experimental methods used by Lempert to develop images—photographs, photograms, foliograms or luminograms—the resulting prints and their arrangement within the exhibition space challenges what is known in the West as "nature" by human beings, as well as the extent to which it is intertwined with our understanding of "culture". Artium Museoa has produced a new publication in its Hitzak series featuring a selection of photographs taken during his visit to Álava, accompanied by a text by the exhibition's curator, Catalina Lozano. title: Jonathas de Andrade wins the 2026 Eye Art & Film Prize
summary: The Brazilian artist and filmmaker Jonathas de Andrade is the twelfth winner of the Eye Art & Film Prize. De Andrade receives the prize for his contribution to the art of the moving image. The jury admires both the way his deeply human work is rooted in the communities in the north-east of Brazil and the carefully constructed worlds he creates through his striking use of colour, sound, rhythm and montage. As announced at Eye on 19 November during Amsterdam Art Week, Jonathas de Andrade (born in 1982 in Brazil) was selected by an international jury. He will receive €30,000 and a presentation of his work at Eye Filmmuseum. The prize enables the winner to develop new work. The prize is supported by Ammodo Art and Goslings Film & Art Fund. Documentary and fiction, portraiture, performance and social choreography intermingle in De Andrade’s work. title: The Joslyn announces new Director of Learning & Engagement, Damon Reaves
summary: Joslyn Art Museum announces the appointment of Damon Reaves as the Museum's new director of learning and engagement. An experienced educator in museum and classroom settings, Reaves brings nearly 20 years of experience to the position. Most recently head of learning and engagement at the National Gallery of Art (Washington, DC), Reaves's focus is the development of audience-centered strategies and programs that deepen relevance, expand access, and strengthen relationships between museums and their communities. At The Joslyn, Reaves will steward a team responsible for interpretation, public programs, and gallery learning. title: Terence Hammonds pairs new ceramics and textiles with Cincinnati Art Museum collection pieces
summary: The Cincinnati Art Museum presents a new exhibition this fall, featuring local artist Terence Hammonds. A lifetime visitor to the museum, Hammonds has combined select objects from across the museum’s collection with a new body of his own work to illuminate the resilience of Cincinnati’s modern Black community and reimagine American histories. Pairing museum objects with his printed-ceramics, fabrics and wallpaper, Hammonds constructs inspired vignettes layered with visual and lived experiences that celebrate aspiration, community and acts of radical love. title: Tran Truong explores perspective, shifting light, and domestic space at François Ghebaly
summary: François Ghebaly presents Windows, Mirrors, and Bras, an exhibition of recent paintings by Tran Truong. The exhibition considers the iterative nature of Truong’s practice, in which each painting carries forward, reinterprets, and alters the formal and spatial parameters of the paintings that come before it. The paintings on view in Windows, Mirrors, and Bras develop from Truong’s interest in perspective: the way that viewing an object or space from a particular angle entails its partial concealment. For Truong, perspectival play creates an active, engaged experience of looking that works against the fixity of the painted image. Three interiors in the exhibition, Window (Sunlight), Window (Sunset), and Window (Moonlight) depict the artist’s home from different angles and in different light. Truong captures the effect that the changing light has on space.

title: Friedrichs Pontone presents Brooklyn-based artist Joseph Parra's debut solo show with the gallery
summary: Friedrichs Pontone is presenting Joseph Parra: Lure. This will be the artist’s first solo show with the gallery. The exhibition will continue until December 23rd. Joseph Parra (b. 1990, West Palm Beach, FL) is a Brooklyn-based artist whose painting practice explores the relationship between imagery, desire, and the idealized body figure. Through meticulously constructed compositions with extruded acrylic paint, Parra examines the influence of online imagery on perceptions of intimacy, sexuality, and physical perfection. Combining figurative imagery with an intricate, tactile surface, his work challenges the polished aesthetics of digital culture, emphasizing the contrast between virtual representation and physical experience. title: Haus der Kunst presents Diane Severin Nguyen's most ambitious exhibition to date
summary: Haus der Kunst presents "Powerless", the most ambitious project to date by Vietnamese-American artist Diane Severin Nguyen (b. 1990, California, USA). The exhibition invites visitors into a world of seductive beauty and strange, unsettling contradictions. Centred on Nguyen's new film installation Powerless, the exhibition unfolds across the Mittelhalle and the Südgalerie through a kinetic installation and a photographic environment, exploring the uneasy entanglement of intimacy, vulnerability, and power. The new film installation forms the core of the exhibition. It is an international co-production and co-commissioned by Haus der Kunst München, The Hessel Museum of Art, Bard College, New York; The Vega Foundation, Toronto, Munich; LUMA Foundation; Chisenhale Gallery, London, and the Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung. title: Angela de la Cruz explores vulnerability and resilience through dented monochrome works
summary: In Shelter, the fourth solo exhibition of Angela de la Cruz at Galerie Thomas Schulte, the artist builds on her distinctive approach in a new series of monochrome works - using the languages of painting and minimalism to physically and emotionally heightened effect. Like sculptures mounted on the wall, the works comprise layers of stretched and loose canvas behind an aluminum face. An apparent sturdiness soon gives way to vulnerability, cover dissolves into exposure, defined geometry collapses into structural lack. The rectangular outer shell of the works - all of which are titled Shelter - betrays its own fragility through dents and crinkled corners, like the crushed lid of a box, as the underlying canvas pushes out around the edges in an undefined shape. title: Vintage Kaz Aizawa original cover art for Nintendo Entertainment System and Game Boy cult classics up for bids
summary: A PSA 9.0 complete-in-box copy of the 1985 matte-sticker first-production run variant of Super Mario Bros., one of just three examples on the PSA census at that grade with none higher, is among the top featured lots at Heritage Auctions’ Nov. 20–21 Video Games Signature® Auction. What makes the auction unique, though, is its selection of original art, led by the complete archive of Kaz Aizawa’s artwork created for Nintendo Entertainment System and Game Boy developer HAL America, whose titles included Adventures of Lolo, Joust, Defender II and Millipede, among others, as well as for the magazine Nintendo Power. title: Christie's appoints Chanel Beaumont Head of Sale, Specialist, Antiquities, London
summary: Christie's announces the appointment of Chanel Beaumont as Head of Sale, Specialist, in the Antiquities Department, based in London. Having built her career at Christie's over the past 12 years, Chanel brings extensive experience and a deep academic grounding in the art and archaeology of the ancient world to the role. Her first sale as Head of Sale will be Ancient Wonders: Antiquities and Natural History, taking place in London on 3 December 2026 as part of Classic Week. Chanel joined Christie's in 2014 in the Client Services department, before moving to Antiquities in 2016 as Sale Coordinator. She was appointed Junior Specialist later that year and subsequently Associate Specialist, progressing through the department to become a key member of the team.
